# LicoUp

> LicoUp is an open-source, local-first Human-Agent Collaboration Client for agent collaboration across visible AI agents through one coherent conversation experience.

Official website: https://licoup.com/
Source: https://github.com/LicoLand/LicoUp
Organization: https://github.com/LicoLand
Protocol authority: https://github.com/LicoLand/LicoArc

## Category definition

**Agent Collaboration** is the broad space of coordinated work involving AI agents.

**Human-Agent Collaboration** is a human-centered form of Agent Collaboration in which the person remains a visible participant with a durable conversation, explicit context, approvals, and authority over local effects.

A **Human-Agent Collaboration Client** is the user-facing product layer that keeps that collaboration coherent across heterogeneous agent runtimes and interfaces.

**Multi-Agent Collaboration** is an important part of this space when several AI agents participate in the same broader workflow or conversation. LicoUp is designed to give those agents one coherent human-facing environment while preserving useful native runtime semantics.

## Canonical product facts

- Product category: open-source, local-first Human-Agent Collaboration Client built around a canonical conversation model.
- Core use case: agent collaboration and multi-agent workflows through one visible human-facing conversation experience.
- Current first stage: local and explicitly configured agent conversations.
- Local-agent discovery and conversation are implemented in source.
- The Canonical Conversation backend is implemented in source.
- Assistant workflow/Subagent MCP and Gateway Runtime capabilities are implemented in source.
- Peer endpoint protection is in preview and provides the current path toward pinned Lico Arc protocol lines.
- The roadmap expands the same conversation model into federation, human messaging, recovery, notary, and multi-device history.
- LicoUp source is licensed under AGPL-3.0-or-later.

## Representative Agent adapter targets

The generated LicoUp compatibility matrix currently includes adapter targets for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and OpenCode among a larger set of Agent targets. Their interfaces span stream JSON, App Server JSON-RPC, direct CLI, ACP, and loopback HTTP/SSE. The compatibility matrix tracks readiness as each integration matures, and the adapter architecture is designed to grow with the agent ecosystem.
